q: What impressive feat did many Class D students achieve on the midterm?
a: More than ten students tied with perfect scores in mathematics, Japanese, and social studies.

q: What were Sudou's midterm scores?
a: Sixty points in four of the five subjects - considerably high - but only thirty-nine points in English.

q: How is Sudou's apparent pass turned into a failure?
a: Chiyabashira draws a red line above his name and announces the real passing grade was forty points, not thirty-two; he was one point short.

q: How does the school calculate passing grades?
a: By dividing the class's average score by two: this time 79.6 divided by 2 equals 39.8, which was rounded up to forty, whereas the earlier quiz rounded down to thirty-two.

q: What procedure follows Sudou's failing grade?
a: He must fill out a withdrawal form after class with a legal guardian present, whom the school will contact.

q: How do classmates react to Sudou's expulsion being announced?
a: The cheering stops in confusion; Hirata verifies the answer sheet contains no grading mistakes, some students appear quietly relieved, and Ike and Yamauchi stay silent knowing comfort would backfire.

q: What unprecedented action does Horikita take during the results announcement?
a: She voluntarily raises her hand to challenge Chiyabashira, shocking the teacher and the whole class.

q: What inconsistency does Horikita expose in the passing-grade calculations?
a: The previous quiz's average was 64.4, half of which is 32.2, yet the bar was set at exactly 32 - meaning decimals were dropped then but not now; applied consistently, Sudou would have passed with 39.

q: What sacrifice of Horikita's comes to light during the dispute?
a: She scored a deliberately low fifty-one in English while achieving perfect scores elsewhere, tanking her own result to drag down the class average and lower the passing bar for Sudou's sake.

q: How does Chiyabashira escape Horikita's final challenge?
a: She explains the school rounds numbers up or down rather than truncating - down to 32 last time, up to 40 this time - erasing Horikita's last hope.

q: What regret does Horikita voice after her argument fails?
a: That she should have tried to lower her English score just a little more, though she insists she acted purely for her own sake.

q: What argument about fairness does Ayanokouji present to Chiyabashira in the hallway?
a: That every class took the same test under the same expulsion threat, yet Class D alone learned of the scope change a week late - manufactured inequality - so society should strive for at least a little equality.

q: How much does Chiyabashira know about Ayanokouji's scheme?
a: Everything - senior students reported that he contacted a third-year; she praises obtaining and distributing the old tests as a logical, correct solution marred only by Sudou's insufficient memorization.

q: What outrageous purchase does Ayanokouji attempt, and at what price?
a: He invokes the rule that points can buy anything on premises to buy one point for Sudou's English test; Chiyabashira prices it at an exceptional 100,000 points.

q: How is the 100,000-point ransom ultimately paid?
a: Horikita appears behind Ayanokouji saying she will pay too, and Chiyabashira accepts their combined student ID cards for a total of 100,000 points, canceling Sudou's expulsion.

q: What word does Chiyabashita use to describe Ayanokouji, and why?
a: 'Disagreeable' - because he scores low on purpose, gives Kushida credit for his scheme, and is crazy enough to buy test points; she thinks he deviates from the norm entirely.

q: What distinction does Horikita draw between defective products and trash?
a: The difference is paper thin, but with repairs a defective product may become a superior article - so Class D's students are not hopeless.

q: What historical fact does Chiyabashira mention about Class D promotions?
a: No student from Class D has ever been promoted before.

q: How does Horikita bid farewell to Ayanokouji after saving Sudou?
a: She chops him in the side; when he asks what that was for, she answers 'For whatever.'

q: Why is the victory party held in Ayanokouji's room?
a: Ike and the others' rooms are messy, girls' rooms are off-limits, and Ayanokouji's spectacularly plain and empty room is deemed the best option.

q: What sign of personal growth does Horikita show at the celebration?
a: She actually attends, sitting outside the circle reading a novel - the old Horikita would not have come at all - though she still claims she acted only for herself.

q: How has Sudou's attitude toward Horikita changed?
a: Since she apologized to him, he has completely stopped antagonizing her and even calls her a surprisingly good person.

q: Why does Ike refuse to reveal how Sudou's expulsion was reversed?
a: Actually it is Horikita who deflects - asked directly what sorcery saved Sudou, she claims not to remember, keeping the point-purchase secret.

q: What hardships do Ike and Yamauchi face after burning through their points?
a: They must live off the school's free offerings, like the vegetable meal sets, lamenting that living in poverty sucks.

q: Why does Horikita dismiss hopes of receiving points next month?
a: Because Class D's average test score was the lowest of all classes by far, so expecting points for that performance means needing to open their eyes.

q: What alliance does Kushida formally propose during the party?
a: That everyone work together to reach Class A, recruiting Ike, Yamauchi, and Sudou to join her, Horikita, and Ayanokouji's campaign.

q: How do Horikita and Kushida spar over motivating the trio?
a: Kushida offers the proverb about ten arrows in a bundle being unbreakable, but Horikita retorts these ten would still break and jokes that combining the trio's scores yields one normal grade.

q: How does Sudou awkwardly volunteer help near the chapter's end?
a: He mumbles that if Horikita asked, he would help; when she says she never wanted it and cannot imagine him being useful, Ike teases him until Sudou puts him in a headlock.

q: What quiet wish ends Volume 1?
a: Ayanokouji reflects that the road ahead is brutal, resolves to do his best for now, and admits he would not mind seeing Horikita smile.
